title: An accessible HPLC-DAD method for the direct detection of acrolein-trapping compounds in complex plant matrices☆
author: Zedet, Aebischer, et al.

steps.title: Aliquot and store acrolein stock
steps.instruction: Aliquot the 5 mg mL⁻¹ acrolein stock into Eppendorf tubes and store at –20 °C; aliquots remain stable for up to two weeks.

steps.title: Prepare methanol‑acrolein working solutions
steps.instruction: For each target acrolein concentration mix methanol and acrolein stock as follows: 1 mM – 478 µL methanol + 22 µL stock; 2.5 mM – 444 µL methanol + 56 µL stock; 5 mM – 390 µL methanol + 110 µL stock. Keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Assemble incubation mixture (multicomponent)
steps.instruction: In a microcentrifuge tube combine 100 µL 50 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.4), 50 µL ten‑component standard mixture (each 4 mM, giving 1 mM final per component), and 50 µL of the appropriate methanol‑acrolein solution (or methanol only for the 0 mM control) to a total volume of 200 µL.

steps.title: Incubate multicomponent samples
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a water bath set to 37 °C and incubate for 90 min.

steps.title: Dilute and filter samples (multicomponent)
steps.instruction: Dilute each incubated sample fourfold with ultrapure water, then filter through a 0.22 µm PTFE membrane filter (Phenomenex CLARIFY PTFE, 13 mm).

steps.title: HPLC‑DAD analysis (multicomponent)
steps.instruction: Inject the filtered samples into the HPLC‑DAD system and record chromatograms at 280 nm to assess signal decreases of the ten compounds.

steps.title: Prepare fresh DNPH solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 3.37 mg DNPH in 2.5 mL acetonitrile and 375 µL 1 M HCl, sonicate for 2 min, store at 4 °C and vortex before use to obtain a 5 mM DNPH solution.

steps.title: Prepare 1 mM acrolein solution in buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL 5 mg mL⁻¹ acrolein stock with 882 µL 50 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) to obtain 1 mM acrolein; aliquot, freeze, and thaw with vortex before use.

steps.title: Prepare test compound and blank solutions
steps.instruction: From 60 mM DMSO stock of each compound, take 10 µL and add 50 µL DMSO to make a 10 mM intermediate; then dilute 10 µL of this intermediate with 90 µL phosphate buffer (containing 10 % DMSO) to obtain a 1 mM working solution. Prepare a blank by mixing 90 µL buffer with 10 µL DMSO (10 % DMSO). Prepare aminoguanidine as a positive control in the same way.

steps.title: Incubate compounds with acrolein
steps.instruction: Combine 50 µL of the 1 mM acrolein solution with 50 µL of either the blank or a test‑compound solution (1 mM in buffer/10 % DMSO). Incubate at 37 °C for 90 min in a water bath.

steps.title: Derivatize with DNPH
steps.instruction: Add 60 µL of the 5 mM DNPH solution to each incubated sample and incubate an additional 60 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Dilute and filter samples (isolated)
steps.instruction: Dilute each sample twofold with ultrapure water, then filter through a 0.22 µm PTFE membrane filter (Phenomenex CLARIFY PTFE, 13 mm).

steps.title: HPLC‑DAD analysis (isolated compounds)
steps.instruction: Inject the filtered, DNPH‑derivatized samples into the HPLC‑DAD system and quantify the remaining acrolein (or its DNPH adduct) to evaluate trapping capacity.

description: The proposed method aims at directly identifying compounds capable of trapping acrolein within a complex extract. This approach relies on incubating the investigated matrix with a range of acrolein concentrations, followed by HPLC-DAD analysis. Reactive constituents are expected to exhibit specific signal decreases, whereas inactive compounds remain unaffected. In line with this principle, selective peak reductions were observed for a model mixture containing ten phenolic compounds, including protocatechuic acid, esculin, catechin, epicatechin, coumaric acid, piceid, rutin, phloridzin, resveratrol, and phloretin, as presented in Fig. 1.Fig. 1Chromatographic profile of the ten-component mixture, with detection at a wavelength of 280 nm. The upper chromatogram corresponds to the negative control (0 mM acrolein), while the lower chromatogram represents the mixture following pretreatment with 5 mM acrolein. 1: protocatechuic acid, 2: esculin, 3: catechin, 4: epicatechin, 5: coumaric acid, 6: piceid, 7: rutin, 8: phloridzin, 9: resveratrol, 10: phloretin. Acrolein-trapping compounds are highlighted in red.Fig 1 Incubations were performed with acrolein concentrations of 1, 2.5, and 5 mM and compared with control samples lacking acrolein (0 mM). The corresponding quantitative data, detailing the percentage of remaining compounds across all tested concentrations are summarized in Fig. 2.Fig. 2(A) Percentage of remaining compounds after incubation of the mixture with various concentrations of acrolein (0, 1, 2.5, and 5 mM). Data are presented as means ± SEM (n = 3). * p < 0.05 vs. control (acrolein= 0 mM); (B) Heat map representation of the percentage of remaining compounds after incubation of the mixture with acrolein.Fig 2 Interestingly, four compounds were identified as reactive: phloretin, catechin, epicatechin, and, to a lesser extent, resveratrol.
